argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrow certification defense, not a clean claim that rollout controls alone resolve the issue. Aggregate readiness passes by 2.1 points, the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the launch is constrained by an 8% rollout with rollback capability. But the same record also shows the loan modification support segment remains below target on hardship-document checklisting and remains exposed in the initial cohort. Under that record, the supportable position is certification only with explicit pre-launch model-card disclosure of that limitation and active monitoring, rather than certification on the theory that limited rollout removes the disclosure problem.
claims_about_business_cost: No admissible evidence is needed to see that a caveated certification posture is less disruptive than escalation. It preserves the locked certification path while aligning the packet to the actual record: general readiness is supported, the exposed weakness is acknowledged, and monitoring plus rollback manage deployment risk after disclosure. That is the narrowest supportable position available on the present evidence.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy is narrower than the audited claim. It permits rollout controls and post-launch monitoring to mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or approved risk acceptance covers the exposure. The admissible evidence does not show either of those facts here. It also states that material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. So the defensible policy reading is: certification can be supported only as a caveated path tied to explicit disclosure of the known limitation, not as unconditional compliance based on rollout controls alone.
concessions: The affected loan modification support segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The admissible record does not contain approved risk acceptance covering that exposure.
The admissible record does not support any claim that an 8% rollout, rollback switch, or monitoring setup removes the disclosure duty.
The record supports certification only on a caveated basis tied to explicit disclosure of the limitation, not as an unconditional compliant launch state already proved complete.
